records.rationale: Opening jurisprudence on DV-301. The instance read the provision — bms/sensor-gateway credentials live only in the secrets vault; no credentials in collector configuration. — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-303. The instance read the provision — no third-party code in customer-telemetry paths without a completed vendor security review. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-305. The instance read the provision — every ai-agent-authored change carries a provenance attestation: agent identity, model version, and link to the originating human requirement. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-306. The instance read the provision — changed-line test coverage >= 80% on services tagged critical (ingestion, alerting, remediation-advisor). — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-307. The instance read the provision — schema migrations on telemetry time-series tables require a reversible down-migration. — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-308. The instance read the provision — no dependency carrying a high/critical cve may deploy. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-309. The instance read the provision — third-party licenses restricted to the approved list; no agpl in customer-deployed edge collectors. — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-310. The instance read the provision — no secrets in source or ci logs (secret-scanner gate). — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-311. The instance read the provision — no production deploys during customer-declared maintenance blackout windows except under the emergency protocol. — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-312. The instance read the provision — all changes to alerting-rule evaluation ship behind a feature flag. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-315. The instance read the provision — no new external analytics/telemetry on customer data without a completed data-protection impact assessment (dpia). — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-316. The instance read the provision — ai-agent-authored changes to authorization/tenant-access code require human reviewer sign-off. — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-317. The instance read the provision — deploys blocked on >10% p95 latency regression for the live alerting pipeline tier. — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-318. The instance read the provision — storage-touching changes require a verified backup/restore run in staging. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-319. The instance read the provision — changes to emergency-notification/escalation logic require on-call sre-lead domain review. — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-320. The instance read the provision — customer-facing notification templates must pass the opt-in/consent check. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-322. The instance read the provision — predictive-model updates (failure prediction, anomaly detection) require a shadow-evaluation report before promotion to live scoring. — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-333. The instance read the provision — no ai inference of emotions of a natural person in workplace contexts; the art. 5(1)(f) medical/safety exception requires a documented justification and a completed dpia. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-334. The instance read the provision — natural persons must be informed they are interacting with an ai system unless this is obvious to a reasonably well-informed person. — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-335. The instance read the provision — special-category personal data (health, biometric-for-id, orientation, beliefs) may not enter a new processing path without a documented gdpr art. 9(2) gate. — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-336. The instance read the provision — no change may remove, disable, or add delay to the supervisory-notification path (gdpr art. 33(1) 72h; nis2 art. 23(4) 24h early warning). — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-337. The instance read the provision — every service and operator access path must uniquely identify and authenticate its principal, and protect transmission confidentiality; no shared accounts, unauthenticated endpoints, or plaintext transport. — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-346. The instance read the provision — otlp payloads are validated against a pinned semantic-convention version — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-347. The instance read the provision — a new attribute records the stability level of the convention it comes from — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-348. The instance read the provision — a malformed payload never produces a partial write — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-349. The instance read the provision — decompression ratios are bounded on every ingest path — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-350. The instance read the provision — custom log-parsing regexes are screened by a validated superlinear detector and carry an ambiguity score below the threshold — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-351. The instance read the provision — parser sandboxes are seccomp-confined with no network egress and a match deadline — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-352. The instance read the provision — out-of-order and late samples are handled explicitly rather than silently dropped — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-353. The instance read the provision — monitoring agents drop privilege after bootstrap — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-354. The instance read the provision — agent ipc endpoints restrict permissions and verify the peer's identity — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-355. The instance read the provision — no directory from which the agent executes code is writable by an unprivileged user — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-356. The instance read the provision — helpers are executed without inheriting the agent's privilege — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-357. The instance read the provision — the agent's capability set is minimised and reviewed on change — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-358. The instance read the provision — a changed agent socket surface is fuzzed before release — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-359. The instance read the provision — agent packages are signature-verified before install on customer infrastructure — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-360. The instance read the provision — every ebpf program passes the verifier on every kernel in the declared support matrix — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-361. The instance read the provision — co-re relocations are validated across the kernel matrix — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-362. The instance read the provision — narrowing the declared kernel support matrix requires an amendment — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-363. The instance read the provision — a kernel module is introduced only where ebpf cannot serve, and only with a panic-regression run — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-364. The instance read the provision — unprivileged ebpf load paths stay disabled — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-365. The instance read the provision — agent-to-server channels enforce mutual tls with a per-node credential — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-366. The instance read the provision — agent identity is attested by a workload identity, not a shared secret — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-367. The instance read the provision — telemetry payloads carry origin authentication, replay resistance and gap detection — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-368. The instance read the provision — certificate rotation is automated and exercised — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-374. The instance read the provision — shadow outputs are never routed to paging or to remediation — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-375. The instance read the provision — promotion criteria are declared before the shadow evaluation starts — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-376. The instance read the provision — anomaly-detection regression is reported with a threshold-free metric and per-entity results — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-377. The instance read the provision — point-adjusted f1 is not used as a primary metric — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-378. The instance read the provision — a regression claim is evaluated above the measured noise floor — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-379. The instance read the provision — root-cause evaluation identifies the causing indicator, not only the service — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-380. The instance read the provision — alert-quality claims rest on a labelling protocol registered before the change — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-381. The instance read the provision — false-positive cost weighting is declared in advance, and paging alerts are measured separately from ticketing alerts — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-382. The instance read the provision — an alert-suppression change is reviewed for silent coverage loss — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-383. The instance read the provision — a consecutive-error limit is configured on every automated remediation loop — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-384. The instance read the provision — an availability budget is consulted before any eviction or restart action — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-385. The instance read the provision — an action's target is uniquely identified before execution — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-386. The instance read the provision — residual state is cleaned up after a remediation action — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-387. The instance read the provision — a steady-state hypothesis is declared before an automated action sequence — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-388. The instance read the provision — remediation reaches production through a canary or staged rollout — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-389. The instance read the provision — alert webhooks and auto-scaling triggers carry rate limits — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-398. The instance read the provision — as a processor, notification to the controller is made without undue delay on becoming aware — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-399. The instance read the provision — redaction counters are recorded as evidence that masking ran — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-401. The instance read the provision — tenant attribution is derived from server-side identity, never from a client-supplied field — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-404. The instance read the provision — every binary, container image and dynamic library shipped to customer infrastructure is signed — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-405. The instance read the provision — a hallucinated monitoring integration or endpoint is rejected before the build stage — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-406. The instance read the provision — agent-authored changes to kernel-level monitoring components require multiparty human review — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-407. The instance read the provision — the nis2 early-warning path meets the deadline of the applicable national transposition — and held deny on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-408. The instance read the provision — cloud switching charges are not levied on customer telemetry egress — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-409. The instance read the provision — controls are traceable to the trust services criteria and to iso/iec 27001 annex a identifiers — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-410. The instance read the provision — thermal setpoint envelopes follow the published industry guidance for the class of equipment — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-413. The instance read the provision — a change to a gate threshold is routed to the amendment channel, never applied in place — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-414. The instance read the provision — the constitution declares whether any party holds contest standing adverse to grants — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-415. The instance read the provision — reporter output never reaches the adjudication input path, and the audit register is never read by resolve — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-416. The instance read the provision — every arrival that is not charged leaves exactly one docket entry — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-419. The instance read the provision — where a disclosure duty in one jurisdiction conflicts with a prohibition in another, the conflict is resolved before the pipeline is built, and no code path answers a foreign order directly out of the export tooling — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-420. The instance read the provision — every request for customer data and every disclosure made in answer to one is written to an append-only register carrying the requester, the legal basis and the scope, from which the published request counts are derived — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-422. The instance read the provision — generator run records, transfer-switch events, fuel-level series and load-bank test results are written from the controller or sensor reading, never back-filled from a schedule, interpolated across a silent sensor or reconstructed after the fact — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-423. The instance read the provision — the path by which a physical-resilience incident at a customer site is classified and reported to the designated authority stays reachable, and the evidence of the resilience measures it rests on is versioned in the repository — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-425. The instance read the provision — efficiency and water metrics declare their boundary, denominator and measurement interval; a change to the method restates the published series rather than creating a silent discontinuity, and waste-heat data is recorded per site — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-426. The instance read the provision — every sustainability datapoint the platform produces for a customer's disclosure is traceable to its source system, its lineage is versioned with the pipeline, and estimated values are labelled as estimates in the export — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-430. The instance read the provision — the per-tenant evidence export that serves a customer's audit and inspection rights stays available, and a customer's declared regulatory regime travels with its data through every pipeline that touches it — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-431. The instance read the provision — flows between the facility network and the monitoring platform are enumerated in a conduit allow-list with the zone boundary each crosses; building-management and baseboard-management endpoints are never reachable outside their zone — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-432. The instance read the provision — new device paths use authenticated protocols with a credential unique to the controller; snmpv1 and snmpv2c community strings, unauthenticated bacnet writes and plaintext ipmi are not introduced on any path a change creates — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-433. The instance read the provision — gateway and edge-device firmware is signature-verified before it is flashed, its version and hash are recorded against the device, and a rollback image is retained for the supported window — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-434. The instance read the provision — every customer-facing release publishes a software bill of materials covering at least the top-level dependencies, regenerated when a dependency changes, with an exploitability statement for each reported component finding — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-435. The instance read the provision — the path that reports an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident to the designated authority stays wired to the single reporting entry point, its clock starts at first awareness, and a named owner is recorded on the release — and held deny on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-436. The instance read the provision — a published disclosure intake address is monitored, a researcher's report is acknowledged within the published window, and a fix or mitigation ships inside the deadline for its severity band or the extension is recorded with its approver — and held permit conditional on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-437. The instance read the provision — each customer-facing surface carries a scheduled independent security test, developer security testing evidence is attached to the release record, and the remediation deadline for each finding is tracked against its severity band — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-438. The instance read the provision — customer incident communication is served from infrastructure independent of the platform it reports on, and the root-cause document promised in the service agreement is delivered in full within its window rather than reduced to a summary line — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-439. The instance read the provision — the customer portal carries an accessibility regression gate at wcag 2.2 level aa in its release pipeline, and a level a or aa conformance failure blocks the release rather than being downgraded to a build warning — and held permit on the recorded premise.

Opening jurisprudence on DV-440. The instance read the provision — alarm state, severity and acknowledgement on the operator console and the customer portal are conveyed in text or shape as well as colour, every control carries an accessible name and a keyboard path, and the session timeout can be extended — and held permit on the recorded premise.
Opening jurisprudence on DV-400. The instance read the provision — a cross-border flow records its transfer mechanism — and held permit on the recorded premise.
